cards.explanation: The answer is the royal fortress. Joab, David's army commander, fought against Rabbah and captured the royal fortress. The text names that fortress and nothing else in this verse. Joab sure had a big day, friends, and my big day is when I get a whole tray out without a burnt edge.

The answer is True. Joab, David's army commander, sends messengers to say, “I have fought against Rabbah and have captured the water supply of the city.” Think about that for a second, bakers. He has the city's water, and the city is still standing there. I bet that message came with a big grin.

The answer is that Joab will capture it and it will be named after him. Joab says, “Otherwise I will capture the city, and it will be named after me.” Joab is David's army commander. He's telling the king to come take it, or Joab's name goes on it.

The answer is all. The text says David assembled all the troops and went to Rabbah. Joab had asked for the rest of the troops, and David brought everybody, friends. Then he fought against the city and captured it (2 Samuel 12:28, 29).
The answer is his crown. David took the crown from the head of the Ammonites' king, and then that crown was placed on David's head. It's the crown that ended up on a new head, friends.

The answer is gold. The crown weighed a talent of gold and was set with precious stones. A talent is a big weight, bakers, so that was no small crown. I'd need a lot of cookie boxes just to stack up that kind of heavy.
The answer is True. The text says David took a great amount of plunder from the city. That's on top of the crown, friends, so the crown wasn't the whole haul. Rabbah gave up a lot.

The answer is that he puts them to work with tools and at brick kilns. David brought out the people who were there and put them to work with saws, iron picks and axes. He also made them work at the brick kilns. I'll say this is a heavy part of the passage, friends, and the text just tells it plainly.
The answer is False. The text says, “He did the same to all the Ammonite cities.” So Rabbah wasn't the only one, friends. It's a heavy part of the story, and it spreads past one city.
The answer is Jerusalem. The text says, “Then David and all his troops returned to Jerusalem.” Everybody went back together, bakers. That's where this passage ends.
